messages:
Marisol: quick RFC follow-up — thinking through the fallback grace window for canary -> main traffic bridging. want a short sync on tradeoffs: immediate hard-failover vs short graceful drain + hedging. key questions: how long should a grace period be, how do we prevent cache poisoning during bridging, and who owns the per-tenant fallback budget?

Ethan: +1. we should treat this like connection draining + token-cache TTL. immediate fail is simplest for correctness but noisy for availability.

Priya: my worry is stateful features (session affinity / kv-cache). if we abruptly switch, user sessions will see cold KV and error spike. graceful drain helps but extends risk window.

Sam: suggestion: two-phase bridge: 1) probe-only warmup (0% traffic) to populate caches, 2) soft-hedging window (mirror + low-weight routing) for N minutes, 3) full cutover. hedging = send to canary and main and race winner wins.

Jules: can we centralize budgets? per-tenant fallback budget makes sense: each tenant has X hedged calls per minute so noisy tenants don't eat global capacity. defaults + overrides in tenant config.

Marisol: agree per-tenant budgets. also need deterministic ordering for fallback priorities (sla tier, region, model-compat). for TTLs: maybe invalidate prefix cache only after canary warmup confirmed.

Ethan: operationally we need clear fast signals to force rollback — e.g., error rate > 3% OR p95 latency > 2x baseline for 2 mins. deploy-bot can auto-scale canary down to 0 weight if triggered.

deploy-bot: noted: automated rollback hook available. policy must be explicit in rollout config.

Priya: about cache poisoning: during soft-hedge we must ensure cached keys are tagged by variant id. otherwise responses from canary might replace main cached responses. config snippet: ```json
{"cache": {"variant_tags": true, "prefix_ttl_s": 300}}
```

Sam: +1 on variant tags. also recommend a short prefix-sticky TTL during bridge (e.g., 60-300s) and a background population probe that issues targeted requests to warm hot paths.

Marisol: how long should the hedging window be? proposal: default 5 minutes for small canaries (<1% traffic), 15m for medium (1-5%), 30m+ for large. open to opinions.

Ethan: those numbers look reasonable. add metric-driven extension: extend if error delta is within noise band and p95 not regressing more than 10%.

Jules: note: longer windows increase the chance of divergent latent state (e.g., DB writes). we should forbid hedging for writes unless we have idempotent write-handles or a write-proxy. read-only features are safe.

Priya: +1. for writes we should do a canary-on-shadow mode: mirror only, never race. then after validation, flip routing.

Sam: interface boundary idea: rollout controller exposes simple policy: {warmup_probe: bool, hedged_window_s: int, variant_cache_tag: bool, write_mode: enum}. runtime implements deterministic routing and cache tagging.

Marisol: i'd like that API to be per-route. product teams can tune per-feature (chat vs embeddings vs rerank). also add an emergency-escape TTL to immediately disable hedging for a tenant.

Ethan: one more: telemetry contract. rollout controller must emit a small set of signals every 10s: canary_weight, canary_errors, canary_latency_p50/p95, mirror_diff_rate, cache_miss_rate_by_variant. these are what the auto-rollback watches.

Priya: and include a sampled request id mapping so we can replay mismatches. e.g., store {req_id -> variant_a_resp, variant_b_resp} for a small fraction.

Jules: ops note: we need a dry-run mode that simulates hedging without sending traffic to canary — useful for perf cost estimation.

Marisol: summary action items: 1) design rollout-policy schema (per-route) with fields Sam listed; 2) implement variant-tagged cache + short TTL logic; 3) per-tenant fallback budgets + emergency escape; 4) telemetry set (Ethan) + rollback hooks in deploy-bot; 5) ban hedged writes unless explicit write-proxy. i'll open a brief RFC PR with proposed schema.

Sam: i can mock a schema and a sample controller API this afternoon.

Ethan: i'll draft the telemetry set and alert thresholds.

Priya: i'll outline cache tagging and the warmup probe pattern with sample probe queries.

Jules: i'll write the tenant-budget proposal and default values.

Marisol: thanks team. small follow-up: can we keep the default hedged_window for reads at 5m and mark writes as mirror-only? if no objections i'll include that in RFC. :thumbsup:

Ethan: :thumbsup:

Priya: fine by me

Jules: thumbs

deploy-bot: rolling-monitor: created monitor r/rollout-1763664321. will emit alerts for configured thresholds.
